allOf.x-sutra-check: a :sync reads either :cdc or a :query with its :cursor
:kind :materialization needs the :object-type it materializes — a materialization is ontology → dataset, so it must name the type whose latest state it carries.

:object-type/:properties belong to a `:kind :materialization` dataset. A dataset fed from OUTSIDE names its feed in :external-source; a dataset fed from the ONTOLOGY names its type here — but it has to say which one it is.

a :kind :materialization dataset takes neither :columns nor :external-source. Its schema comes from the ontology definitions and its rows come from the object type — an external feed would make it a second, disagreeing producer of the same table. Use :properties to carry a subset.
a `:kind :materialization` dataset cannot carry `:stream`. A materialization's rows come FROM the ontology, so there is no buffer in front of them to publish into.

`:kind :virtual` and `:virtual {:source … :table …}` go together. A virtual dataset holds no rows of its own — `:virtual` names the source table every read of it scans — so one without the other names nothing or is never read.
a `:kind :virtual` dataset takes neither `:external-source` nor `:stream`. Its rows are the source table's, read in place; a feed would make it a second producer of rows it does not store.

`:kind :restricted-view` and `:restricted-view {:dataset … :policy …}` go together, and such a dataset takes no `:columns`, `:external-source`, `:stream` or `:virtual`. A restricted view holds no rows: every read of it is its backing dataset's rows, filtered by the policy for whoever reads.

a `:stream` dataset needs `:columns`. A stream is inherently tabular and inherently structured — the schema is what a published record is validated against, and without it every batch would be admitted unread.
`:stream :primary-key :deletion-column` has to be one of the declared `:columns` — it is read off each record to decide whether that record RETRACTS its key.
every `:stream` key column has to be one of the declared `:columns`. A key naming a column that does not exist is an ordering guarantee that silently is not one.

allOf.x-sutra-check: an :object / :object-set / :graph parameter must name its :object-type — without it nothing can say which properties the body may reach, and a typo becomes an empty render instead of an error
:object-type belongs to an :object, :object-set or :graph parameter
:object-set belongs to an :object or :object-set parameter
:edge belongs to a :graph parameter and names the link SIDE the edges run along, as seen from the :object-type
a :graph parameter names the link side its edges run along (:edge) — objects without a link between them are a list, and a list is an :object-set
:layout / :richtung belong to a :graph parameter — they say how it is arranged, and nothing else is arranged
only a :graph parameter may name SEVERAL :object-type / :edge — an :object is one object and an :object-set one type's objects; a CHAIN of types is a drawing
a :graph parameter takes no :required, :default or :preview — it is READ from the ontology, never passed in, so there is nothing to demand of a caller and nothing to stand in for it
:via is now :search-around and names link SIDES — their API names as seen from the reached type

:search-around and :of travel together — :search-around names the link sides to walk and :of the :object parameter to walk them from. One without the other says where to go and not from where, or the reverse.
:search-around/:of belong to an :object-set parameter. A single :object is named by its id; a SET that follows a link is the thing that cannot be.
